questions.title: Visual field defect of a pituitary tumour
questions.question: Regarding a tumour of the pituitary gland, one of the following is true:

options.A: It induces a decrease of the intracranial pressure.

explanations.A: Incorrect. An expanding intracranial mass tends to raise, not lower, intracranial pressure; a decrease is not a feature of a pituitary tumour.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Homonymous hemianopia results from a lesion behind the optic chiasma (optic tract or radiation), not from a midline chiasmatic compression.
explanations.C: Correct. The pituitary lies immediately below the optic chiasma, so an enlarging adenoma presses on the crossing nasal retinal fibres in the chiasma. Loss of these fibres removes the temporal halves of both visual fields, producing the classic bitemporal (heteronymous) hemianopia.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cerebellar ataxia arises from posterior-fossa (cerebellar) disease and has no anatomical relationship to a sellar pituitary mass.

questions.learning_objective: Explain why a pituitary tumour classically produces a bitemporal hemianopia by compressing the optic chiasma.

questions.title: Blood supply of the anterior lobe of the pituitary
questions.question: Regarding the blood supply of the pituitary gland, one of the following is true:

options.A: Inferior hypophyseal artery supplies the anterior lobe.
options.B: The hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal circulation supplies the anterior lobe.
options.C: Superior hypophyseal artery supplies the anterior lobe directly.
options.D: Its venous drainage is into the superior sagittal venous sinus.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The inferior hypophyseal artery supplies the posterior lobe (neurohypophysis), not the anterior lobe.
explanations.B: Correct. The superior hypophyseal arteries first form a capillary plexus in the median eminence and infundibulum; blood then drains into hypophyseal portal veins that carry it down to a second sinusoidal capillary bed in the anterior lobe. So the adenohypophysis receives almost all of its blood indirectly through this portal circulation rather than from an artery directly.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superior hypophyseal artery does not supply the anterior lobe directly; it drains first into the portal veins, which then perfuse the anterior lobe.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Venous blood from the pituitary drains into the neighbouring cavernous sinuses, not the superior sagittal sinus.

questions.learning_objective: Describe how the hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal circulation supplies the anterior lobe of the pituitary.

questions.title: Relations of the pituitary gland (the wrong statement)
questions.question: Regarding the relations of the pituitary gland, one of the following is WRONG:

options.A: It lies above the diaphragma sellae.
options.C: It is related laterally to the internal carotid artery.
options.D: It lies above the body of the sphenoid.

explanations.A: Correct (this is the wrong statement). The diaphragma sellae is a dural roof over the hypophyseal fossa, pierced by the infundibulum. The gland lies BELOW the diaphragma sellae, not above it, so this statement is false and is the answer to a 'which is WRONG' stem.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this statement is true). The hypothalamus lies above the gland and is connected to it by the infundibular stalk through the diaphragma sellae.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this statement is true). On each side of the hypophyseal fossa the cavernous sinus, with the internal carotid artery running through it, is a lateral relation of the pituitary.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this statement is true). The fossa sits in the body of the sphenoid, which lies below the gland.

questions.learning_objective: State that the pituitary gland lies below the diaphragma sellae, with the hypothalamus above and the sphenoid body below.

questions.title: Medial relation of the thyroid lobe
questions.question: Regarding the relations of the thyroid gland, one of the following is TRUE:

options.A: It is related to the superior laryngeal nerve.
options.B: It is related posteriorly to the external carotid artery.
options.C: It is related medially to the trachea and oesophagus.
options.D: It is related to the middle constrictor muscle of the pharynx.

explanations.A: Incorrect. It is the external laryngeal nerve (running with the superior thyroid artery) and the recurrent laryngeal nerve that are the surgically important relations, not the trunk of the superior laryngeal nerve.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The gland is not related posteriorly to the external carotid; the carotid sheath (common carotid) lies posterolateral to the lobe.
explanations.C: Correct. The medial surface of each thyroid lobe is moulded on two tubes, the trachea and oesophagus, together with the two cartilages (thyroid and cricoid), the cricothyroid and inferior constrictor muscles, and the recurrent laryngeal and external laryngeal nerves. Trachea and oesophagus are therefore true medial relations.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inferior constrictor (not the middle constrictor) is a medial relation of the thyroid lobe; the middle constrictor is higher, at the level of the hyoid.

questions.learning_objective: List the trachea and oesophagus as medial relations of the thyroid lobe.

questions.title: Posterior relation of the thyroid lobe
questions.question: Regarding the relations of the thyroid gland, one of the following is true:

options.A: It is related to the internal laryngeal nerve.
options.B: It is related posteriorly to the inferior thyroid artery.
options.C: It is related posteriorly to the thyroid and cricoid cartilages.
options.D: It is related anteriorly to the parathyroid gland.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The internal laryngeal nerve pierces the thyrohyoid membrane above the gland and is not a relation of the thyroid lobe.
explanations.B: Correct. The posteromedial aspect of the lobe carries the inferior thyroid artery (a branch of the thyrocervical trunk) and its close companion the recurrent laryngeal nerve, along with the parathyroid glands. The inferior thyroid artery is therefore a posterior relation of the lobe.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The thyroid and cricoid cartilages lie medial to the lobe, not posterior.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The parathyroid glands are embedded on the POSTERIOR (posteromedial) surface of the lobe, not anteriorly.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the inferior thyroid artery as a posterior relation of the thyroid lobe.

questions.title: Relations of the isthmus of the thyroid gland
questions.question: Regarding the relations of the isthmus of the thyroid gland, one of the following is true:

options.A: It is related superiorly to the anastomosis of the superior thyroid arteries.
options.B: It is related posteriorly to the 6th, 7th and 8th tracheal rings.
options.C: It is related below to the inferior thyroid arteries.
options.D: It is related anteriorly to the sternomastoid muscle.

explanations.A: Correct. The isthmus connects the two lobes across the front of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th tracheal rings. Its upper border is crossed by the anastomosing branches of the two superior thyroid arteries, so the superior thyroid arterial anastomosis is a superior relation of the isthmus.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The isthmus lies on the 2nd to 4th tracheal rings, not the 6th to 8th.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The inferior thyroid veins (not arteries) leave the lower border of the isthmus; the inferior thyroid arteries reach the lobes posteriorly.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Anteriorly the isthmus is covered by the strap muscles (sternohyoid and sternothyroid) and the pretracheal fascia, not the sternomastoid, which lies more laterally.

questions.learning_objective: Relate the upper border of the thyroid isthmus to the anastomosis of the superior thyroid arteries.

questions.title: Origin of the inferior thyroid artery
questions.question: Regarding the blood supply of the thyroid gland, one of the following is true:

options.A: The superior thyroid artery supplies the upper two thirds of the lobe.
options.B: The inferior thyroid artery supplies the lower one third of the lobe.
options.C: The superior thyroid artery is a branch of the internal carotid artery.
options.D: The inferior thyroid artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior thyroid artery mainly supplies the upper pole and the antero-superior part of the lobe, not a clean upper two thirds; the two arteries anastomose freely within the gland.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The inferior thyroid artery supplies the lower pole and, importantly, most of the posterior part of the gland and the parathyroids, not merely a lower one third.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superior thyroid artery is the first branch of the EXTERNAL carotid artery, not the internal carotid.
explanations.D: Correct. The inferior thyroid artery arises from the thyrocervical trunk, a branch of the first part of the subclavian artery, and ascends to reach the lower pole and posterior surface of the lobe. This is the standard origin tested here.

questions.learning_objective: State that the inferior thyroid artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk.

questions.title: Superior thyroid artery and the external laryngeal nerve
questions.question: Regarding the blood supply of the thyroid gland, one of the following is true:

options.A: The superior thyroid artery is related to the external laryngeal nerve.
options.B: In thyroidectomy the superior thyroid artery is ligated away from the gland.
options.C: The thyroidea ima artery is found in all persons.
options.D: In thyroidectomy the inferior thyroid artery is ligated close to the gland.

explanations.A: Correct. As the superior thyroid artery descends to the upper pole it runs with the external laryngeal nerve, which supplies the cricothyroid. Because the two are so close, the artery must be ligated CLOSE to the gland at the apex to avoid injuring the nerve, which would weaken the voice.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The superior thyroid artery is ligated close to the gland (near the upper pole), precisely to keep the ligature away from the external laryngeal nerve, not away from the gland.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The thyroidea ima is an inconstant artery present in only a minority of people, not in all persons.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inferior thyroid artery is ligated AWAY from the gland (laterally) to avoid the recurrent laryngeal nerve, which lies near the gland; ligating it close to the gland risks the nerve.

questions.learning_objective: Relate the superior thyroid artery to the external laryngeal nerve and explain the ligation rules in thyroidectomy.

questions.title: Preserving the parathyroids in thyroidectomy
questions.question: Regarding the parathyroid glands, one of the following is true:

options.A: They are supplied by the superior thyroid artery.
options.B: In thyroidectomy the posterior part of the thyroid gland is not removed, to preserve them.
options.C: The thyroidea ima artery supplies them.
options.D: The inferior parathyroid gland has the same position in all persons.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The parathyroids are supplied mainly by the inferior thyroid artery (with some contribution from anastomoses), not principally the superior thyroid artery.
explanations.B: Correct. The parathyroid glands lie on the posterior surface of the thyroid lobe within its capsule. In subtotal thyroidectomy the surgeon deliberately leaves the posterior part of each lobe undisturbed so as to preserve the parathyroid glands and their blood supply and avoid post-operative hypocalcaemia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The thyroidea ima is an inconstant artery to the isthmus/lower thyroid; it is not the supply of the parathyroids.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inferior parathyroid is the more variable of the two in position; its site is not constant, whereas the superior parathyroid is relatively constant.

questions.learning_objective: Explain that the posterior part of the thyroid lobe is preserved in thyroidectomy to protect the parathyroid glands.

questions.title: Shape of the left suprarenal gland
questions.question: Regarding the suprarenal glands, one of the following is true:

options.A: The left gland is triangular in shape.
options.B: The left gland is semilunar in shape.
options.C: The left gland does not reach the hilum of the left kidney.
options.D: The left gland has 3 arteries and 3 veins.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A pyramidal/triangular outline belongs to the RIGHT suprarenal gland; the left is crescentic.
explanations.B: Correct. The left suprarenal gland is semilunar (crescentic) in shape and is the larger, more medially placed of the two. It caps the upper pole and extends down along the medial border of the left kidney towards its hilum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The left gland does reach down along the medial border towards the hilum of the left kidney; it is the left gland that comes close to the hilum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Each suprarenal has THREE arteries (superior, middle, inferior) but only ONE vein, not three veins.

questions.learning_objective: State that the left suprarenal gland is semilunar in shape.

questions.title: Shape of the right suprarenal gland
questions.question: Regarding the suprarenal glands, one of the following is true:

options.A: The right gland is triangular (pyramidal) in shape.
options.B: The right gland is semilunar in shape.
options.C: The right gland reaches the hilum of the right kidney.
options.D: The right gland has 3 arteries and 3 veins.

explanations.A: Correct. The right suprarenal gland is pyramidal (triangular) in shape and sits like a cap on the upper pole of the right kidney, tucked behind the inferior vena cava. The crescentic (semilunar) shape is the left gland.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Semilunar/crescentic is the LEFT gland; the right is pyramidal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The right gland caps the upper pole and does not reach down to the hilum; it is the left gland that approaches the renal hilum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Each suprarenal gland has three arteries but only one vein.

questions.learning_objective: State that the right suprarenal gland is pyramidal (triangular) in shape.

questions.title: Anterior relations of the right suprarenal gland
questions.question: Regarding the suprarenal glands, one of the following is true:

options.A: The right gland is covered anteriorly by the IVC and the right lobe of the liver.
options.B: The right gland is semilunar in shape.
options.C: The right gland reaches the hilum of the right kidney.
options.D: The hilum of the right gland is directed downward.

explanations.A: Correct. The anterior surface of the right suprarenal gland is overlapped medially by the inferior vena cava and laterally by the bare area of the right lobe of the liver. This intimate relation to the IVC is why the short right suprarenal vein draining straight into the cava is a surgical hazard.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The right gland is pyramidal, not semilunar (that is the left gland).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The right gland caps the upper pole and does not reach the hilum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The hilum of the right suprarenal gland faces roughly anteromedially and drains into the IVC; it is not directed straight downward.

questions.learning_objective: List the inferior vena cava and the right lobe of the liver as anterior relations of the right suprarenal gland.

questions.title: Arteries and veins of the suprarenal gland (the wrong statement)
questions.question: Regarding the suprarenal glands, one of the following is WRONG:

options.A: The upper suprarenal artery arises from the inferior phrenic artery.
options.B: The middle suprarenal artery arises from the abdominal aorta.
options.C: The lower suprarenal artery arises from the renal artery.
options.D: The suprarenal vein of both sides ends in the IVC.

explanations.A: Incorrect (this statement is true). The superior suprarenal artery is a branch of the inferior phrenic artery.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this statement is true). The middle suprarenal artery arises directly from the abdominal aorta.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this statement is true). The inferior suprarenal artery is a branch of the renal artery.
explanations.D: Correct (this is the wrong statement). Only the RIGHT suprarenal vein drains into the inferior vena cava; the LEFT suprarenal vein drains into the left renal vein. So it is false that the vein of both sides ends in the IVC.

questions.learning_objective: Contrast the three suprarenal arteries with the venous drainage, where the left suprarenal vein ends in the left renal vein and the right in the IVC.

questions.title: Surface location of the pancreas
questions.question: Regarding the site of the pancreas, one of the following is true:

options.A: It lies in the epigastrium only.
options.B: It lies in the left hypochondrium only.
options.C: It lies in the epigastrium and the left hypochondrium.
options.D: It lies in the right hypochondrium only.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The head and neck occupy the epigastrium, but the body and tail extend to the left, so it is not confined to the epigastrium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Only the tail reaches the left hypochondrium; the bulk of the gland is more medial.
explanations.C: Correct. The pancreas lies transversely across the posterior abdominal wall at roughly the L1-L2 level: the head, neck and body occupy the epigastric region while the tail passes into the left hypochondrium to reach the hilum of the spleen. It therefore spans the epigastrium and the left hypochondrium.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The pancreas does not lie in the right hypochondrium; that region is occupied mainly by the liver.

questions.learning_objective: State that the pancreas lies in the epigastrium and the left hypochondrium.

questions.title: The common bile duct behind the head of the pancreas
questions.question: Regarding the pancreas, one of the following is true:

options.B: Its head lies behind the liver.
options.C: The common bile duct runs behind the head.
options.D: Its body lies behind the abdominal aorta.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The pancreas is described in four (or five) parts: head (with uncinate process), neck, body and tail, not three.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The head lies within the C-shaped concavity of the duodenum, not behind the liver.
explanations.C: Correct. As the common bile duct descends it grooves or is embedded in the posterior surface of the head of the pancreas before it opens, with the main pancreatic duct, into the second part of the duodenum. This posterior relation is why carcinoma of the head causes obstructive jaundice.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The body of the pancreas lies IN FRONT of (anterior to) the abdominal aorta, not behind it.

questions.learning_objective: State that the common bile duct runs behind the head of the pancreas.

questions.title: Relation of the tail of the pancreas to the spleen
questions.question: Regarding the pancreas, one of the following is true:

options.A: The portal vein begins in front of its neck.
options.B: Its tail is related to the spleen.
options.C: Its body lies behind the left kidney.
options.D: Its duct opens at the 3rd part of the duodenum.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The portal vein begins BEHIND the neck of the pancreas, by the union of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins, not in front of it.
explanations.B: Correct. The tail of the pancreas is the only part that is intraperitoneal; it runs in the splenorenal (lienorenal) ligament together with the splenic vessels and reaches the hilum of the spleen. The tail is therefore closely related to the spleen.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The body lies in front of the left kidney and the left suprarenal gland, not behind the kidney.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The main duct opens at the greater duodenal papilla in the second part of the duodenum, not the third part.

questions.learning_objective: State that the tail of the pancreas is related to the hilum of the spleen in the splenorenal ligament.

questions.title: Termination of the main pancreatic duct
questions.question: Regarding the main pancreatic duct, one of the following is true:

options.A: It is formed only by the duct of the dorsal pancreatic bud.
options.B: It crosses the accessory pancreatic duct in the head of the pancreas.
options.C: It opens at the middle of the posterolateral aspect of the 3rd part of the duodenum.
options.D: It joins the common bile duct to form the hepatopancreatic ampulla.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The main pancreatic duct (of Wirsung) is formed mainly from the duct of the VENTRAL bud plus the distal part of the dorsal duct, not the dorsal duct alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The accessory duct (of Santorini) drains the upper head and opens separately at the minor papilla; the two ducts do not cross in this way.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The main duct opens at the greater duodenal papilla on the posteromedial wall of the SECOND part of the duodenum, not the middle of the third part.
explanations.D: Correct. Near its termination the main pancreatic duct is joined by the common bile duct. Together they form the dilated hepatopancreatic ampulla (of Vater). This opens on the summit of the major duodenal papilla in the second part of the duodenum, guarded by the sphincter of Oddi.

questions.learning_objective: Describe how the main pancreatic duct joins the common bile duct to form the hepatopancreatic ampulla.
